proposals.before: When the High Ancestor secured the capital and set up his headquarters, Dun joined the staff of General of Agile Cavalry as penal and judicial aide.
proposals.after: When the High Ancestor secured the capital and set up his headquarters, Weizhen was brought onto the staff of General of Agile Cavalry as penal and judicial aide.
proposals.reason: Chinese silent subject continues Zang Weizhen's career; English wrongly names Dun.

proposals.before: When the High Ancestor pacified the capital region and established the hegemon's headquarters, Dun was brought in as penal and judicial aide on the staff of General of Agile Cavalry.
proposals.after: When the High Ancestor pacified the capital region and established the hegemon's headquarters, Weizhen was brought in as penal and judicial aide on the staff of General of Agile Cavalry.
proposals.reason: Chinese silent subject continues Weizhen; English wrongly inserts Dun.

proposals.before: His father Weizhen was broadly learned in letters and history and gifted in affairs; in youth he won the notice of his maternal uncle Zhou Yong of Runan.
proposals.after: His father Weizhen was broadly learned in letters and history and gifted in affairs; in youth he won the notice of his maternal cousin Zhou Yong of Runan.
proposals.reason: 外兄 is maternal cousin, not maternal uncle.

proposals.before: His father Hui, under Heavenly Surveillance, held Shan and Jiankang in succession, likewise famed for ability, and reached staff adviser to Rapid Cavalry.
proposals.after: His father Hui, under Heavenly Surveillance, held Shanyin and Jiankang in succession, likewise famed for ability, and reached staff adviser to Rapid Cavalry.
proposals.reason: 山陰 was mistranslated as Shan; restore Shanyin.

proposals.before: At that time the northern suburban altar was being rebuilt; Qi was first put in charge of construction, and when the work was finished he was appointed as if under the new regulations.
proposals.after: At that time the northern suburban altar was being rebuilt; Qi was first put in charge of construction, and when the work was finished he was appointed magistrate of Ruxin.
proposals.reason: 除如新令 means appointed magistrate of Ruxin (如新), not 'as if under the new regulations'.

proposals.before: At that time the northern suburban altar was being newly built; Qi was first put in charge of supervising construction, and when the work was done he was appointed as if under the new regulations.
proposals.after: At that time the northern suburban altar was being newly built; Qi was first put in charge of supervising construction, and when the work was done he was appointed magistrate of Ruxin.
proposals.reason: 除如新令 is a county appointment to Ruxin, not a regulatory phrase.

decisions.reason: s0006 introduces 父未甄 and s0007–s0009 continue that career with a silent subject; 引爲 does not name Dun, so the idiomatic English wrongly inserts him.
The same silent subject after 父未甄 is Weizhen; the literal’s named Dun is not in the Chinese and must be corrected to Weizhen.

decisions.reason: 外兄 is a maternal cousin, not a maternal uncle (舅); the literal’s uncle rendering invents the wrong kinship grade.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 少爲外兄汝南周顒所知

decisions.reason: 歷山陰、建康令 names the county 山陰 (Shanyin), already correctly rendered in s0068; cutting it to Shan is a place-name error.
除如新令 is the standard appointment formula for magistrate (令) of the county 如新; s0074’s 縣民 confirms a county post, not ‘new regulations’.
The literal likewise misreads 除如新令; the Chinese appoints Fu Qi magistrate of Ruxin, matching the following county-case narrative.
